inputs.status: Conceptual redesign of S7 at the owner's direction; not engineering-qualified
changes_from_S7: Two gravity discs inline in tandem along the flight direction, edge-on, with parallel counterrotating spin axes perpendicular to flight
Discs lock during burns; thrust lies in the disc plane and each room reconfigures so 'down' faces the thrusting engine

Braking fuel is built into each gravity disc's walls (rim and both faces) as nested tank layers that turn with the disc, consumed outermost first; disc spacing and corridor height grow with the wall thickness
Forward shield resized to the new frontal envelope at the S7 areal allocation; mass and fuel ledger recalculated to convergence

Main engine on 2000 m tow tethers: ahead and pulling through acceleration, re-rigged behind and pulling backward for braking. One forward dust shield, always at the leading end: in front of the engine while it leads, moved to the front of the ship when the engine is re-rigged behind. Dust arrives along the axis, so its shadow covers everything behind it; the four pod engines sit in a row across the shield's width so they fit its outline; four nozzle pods canted outward just enough for the plume edge to clear the ship; the thrust lost to the cant is charged to the fuel ledger
Tank volumes from liquid storage densities rather than a symbol scale

storage.status: Liquid D2 near 20 K and liquid He-3 near its 3.2 K boiling point; no ullage, insulation, wall or cryocooler volume (optimistic). Antihydrogen as solid ice, containment volume excluded.

habitat.status: Pressure hulls the fuel walls wrap. rim_gap_m is kept between the outer walls of the two discs for the food trains; the transfer corridor rides above the top walls. The food trains and corridor are despun part-time spaces outside the walls.

shielding.target_status: null = put all braking fuel in the walls. Only braking fuel remains aboard through the coast; likely below what a 20-year interstellar GCR dose budget needs; transport analysis still required. Set a number to wrap only that much and stage the remainder aft.
shielding.material_note: Deuterium (Z/A 0.5) and helium-3 (Z/A 0.67) shield per gram roughly like water or polyethylene, not like hydrogen (Z/A 1.0).

forward_shield.shape: Rectangle covering the shell's frontal envelope

tow.status: Zylon-class fibre at its nominal strength with a safety factor of 2 (owner selection; 3 would add about 3,000 t at departure), sized for departure thrust. Tethers carry the engine's pull; tension straps hang the habitat and every tank module below the tow frame, so no long member is in compression. Tether dynamics, re-rigging between burns, abrasion, damage tolerance and creep are unsized. Nozzle cant is the smallest that keeps the plume edge (assumed 5 degree half-angle: residual ion thermal spread of a ~100 keV plasma at 0.08c exhaust, not a nozzle design) a 5 m margin clear of the ship; its thrust loss (1 - cos) is charged to the fuel ledger.

added_crew_hardware: Transfer-tube windows (in place of a cupola)
EVA handrails, tether points and small robotic arm (suits and airlocks are the habitats' own)

surface_solar.storage_note: Four hours at an assumed 125 kW critical load, with crop lighting and workshop loads shed.
surface_solar.heat_rejection_note: Fan-driven air-cooled dry coolers using the atmosphere the entry already relies on; planning figure.
surface_solar.status: Replaces the antimatter power plant: the settlement is in permanent daylight on the tidally locked day side, so storage only rides through flares and dust. Top-of-atmosphere irradiance from Ribas et al. (2017), with an assumed surface transmission. Crop lighting uses no daylight credit. Very thin roll-out photovoltaic blankets (thin-film on polyimide) unrolled flat on the graded ground with pegged edges and printed busbars, no frames; flat panels see the star at 45 degrees, so flux is reduced by sin(45). Masses are planning assumptions. Replaces the 15 t 'Surface power and services' allocation on the cargo ship.

fuel_feed.status: Cryogenic feed along the tether to a buffer tank at the engine; sized for peak flow at departure. Mass is inside the S7 'Fixed main-feed and deployment services' allocation (not resized).
